phases.title: The nuclear deal
phases.sum: Iran agreed with six powers to limit its nuclear program in return for the lifting of nuclear sanctions.
phases.detail: On 14 July 2015 Iran, the US, the UK, France, Germany, Russia, China and the EU agreed the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) in Vienna. On 20 July 2015 the UN Security Council endorsed it in Resolution 2231. On 16 January 2016, Implementation Day, the IAEA reported that Iran had taken its first nuclear steps under the deal. The same day the US stopped applying its nuclear-related sanctions and the EU lifted its own. On 8 May 2018 President Trump announced that the US was leaving the deal and would reimpose its sanctions.

phases.title: Maximum pressure
phases.sum: The US restored its sanctions and listed the Revolutionary Guards as a terrorist group; tankers and Saudi oil plants were attacked in 2019.
phases.detail: After the US exit on 8 May 2018, US sanctions returned in two steps, the last when the 180-day wind-down ended on 4 November 2018. On 5 November 2018 the Treasury listed more than 700 people, firms, aircraft and vessels, its largest single action on Iran. On 8 April 2019 the US named the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps a Foreign Terrorist Organization. On 12 May 2019 four tankers were damaged off Fujairah, and on 13 June 2019 two tankers were hit in the Gulf of Oman; the US blamed Iran, which denied it. On 14 September 2019 drones and missiles hit Saudi Aramco's plants at Abqaiq and Khurais. The US said the attack came from Iran; the Houthis claimed it.

phases.title: Soleimani and the shadow war
phases.sum: A US strike killed Qasem Soleimani; Iran's nuclear program was hit by a killing and sabotage, and Iran raised enrichment to 60%.
phases.detail: On 3 January 2020 a US strike at Baghdad airport killed Qasem Soleimani, the head of the Quds Force. On 27 November 2020 nuclear scientist Mohsen Fakhrizadeh was killed near Tehran; Iran blamed Israel, which did not comment. On 11 April 2021 an explosion cut power at the Natanz enrichment plant. On 16 April 2021 Iran began enriching uranium to 60%, its highest level until then, and the IAEA confirmed it. On 16 September 2022 Mahsa Amini died after her arrest by the morality police, and protests spread across Iran. On 10 March 2023 Saudi Arabia and Iran agreed in Beijing to restore relations.

phases.title: Gaza and the first direct blows
phases.sum: The Gaza war opened the axis fronts; Iran and Israel struck each other directly for the first time, in April and October 2024.
phases.detail: On 7 October 2023 Hamas attacked Israel and the Gaza war began; Hezbollah opened fire on 8 October 2023. On 1 April 2024 a strike on Iran's consulate in Damascus killed IRGC commanders, and on the night of 13–14 April Iran launched more than 300 drones and missiles at Israel, its first direct attack. On 31 July 2024 Hamas leader Ismail Haniyeh was killed in Tehran, and on 27 September 2024 Israel killed Hezbollah leader Hassan Nasrallah in Beirut. On 1 October 2024 Iran fired more than 180 ballistic missiles at Israel, by Israel's count; on 26 October Israel struck air defences and missile plants in Iran. An Israel–Lebanon ceasefire took effect on 27 November 2024. On 8 December 2024 rebels took Damascus and Bashar al-Assad fled Syria.

phases.title: Talks and the twelve-day war
phases.sum: US–Iran talks were under way when Israel attacked Iran on 13 June 2025; the US bombed three nuclear sites before a ceasefire on 24 June.
phases.detail: From April 2025 the US and Iran held rounds of talks mediated by Oman, and a sixth round was due in June. On 12 June 2025 the IAEA Board of Governors found Iran in breach of its safeguards obligations, by 19 votes to 3 with 11 abstentions. On 13 June 2025 Israel struck Iran's nuclear and military sites and Iran fired missiles at Israel. On 22 June the US bombed Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan. On 23 June Iran fired missiles at the Al Udeid base in Qatar. Trump announced a ceasefire that evening, and it took effect on 24 June.

phases.title: Snapback and the road to war
phases.sum: UN sanctions returned in September 2025; protests were crushed in January 2026, and talks resumed in February as US forces gathered.
phases.detail: On 28 August 2025 the UK, France and Germany triggered the UN "snapback". On 19 September 2025 a Security Council draft to keep sanctions relief failed, and the UN sanctions returned on 27 September (28 September GMT). Protests began on 28 December 2025 with a strike at the Tehran bazaar as the rial fell. By 26 January 2026 the rights group HRANA counted at least 6,126 dead in the crackdown; the government put the toll at 3,117. US–Iran talks resumed in Muscat on 6 February 2026 and moved to Geneva later that month, while the US built up its forces in the region. On 27 February 2026 Trump authorised the strikes.

now.title: Lion's Roar and Epic Fury
now.sum: Since US–Israeli strikes killed Ali Khamenei on 28 February, the war has spread to Lebanon, Iraq, the Gulf states and the Strait of Hormuz; a June deal collapsed on 8 July, attacks resumed in September, and on 8 October Trump said there would be no US strikes before the 3 November elections.
now.detail:
Iran, Israel and the US: On 28 February 2026 the US and Israel struck Iran and killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei; Iran fired missiles at Israel and at US bases across the region. On 8–9 March the Assembly of Experts named his son Mojtaba Khamenei supreme leader. On 17 March Israel killed Ali Larijani, and on 21 March the US struck Natanz with bunker-busters while Iran hit Dimona. On 3 April Iran shot down a US F-15E. Israel struck Tehran, Isfahan and Tabriz again on 8 June. After the June deal collapsed, US Central Command struck 80 targets in Iran on 8 July. The two sides resumed attacks in early September, and on 8 October Trump said there would be no US strikes before the 3 November midterm elections. On 23 October IAEA chief Rafael Grossi called for inspectors to return to Iran.

Lebanon: Hezbollah opened fire on 2 March, and Israel began ground operations in the south on 16 March. On 8 April, the first day of the US–Iran ceasefire, Israel launched its heaviest strikes on Lebanon of the war. A ten-day Israel–Lebanon truce began on 16 April and was extended; a renewed Israel–Hezbollah truce was announced on 19 June. On 26 June Israel and Lebanon signed a framework in Washington that includes disarming Hezbollah, which Hezbollah rejected. Israel handed parts of its buffer zone to the Lebanese army on 20 July, but strikes and clashes went on. On 3 September Israel said it held the Ali al-Taher ridge, and in early October its forces in the south prepared winter positions.

Iraq: Iran-aligned militias attacked US sites in Erbil and Baghdad from 28 February, striking the US embassy in Baghdad at least four times by late April. On 14 March Kata'ib Hezbollah security chief Abu Ali al-Askari was killed in a strike in Baghdad; the group announced his death on 16 March. On 25 March an air strike on the Habbaniya base killed seven Iraqi soldiers, Iraq's defence ministry said; no one claimed it, the US denied targeting Iraqi forces, and Baghdad summoned the US chargé d'affaires. By late April US and Israeli strikes had hit militia targets in eight provinces.

The Gulf states: On 28 February Iran fired at US bases and cities in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, the UAE and Saudi Arabia. On 1 March six US soldiers were killed by a drone near Port Shuaiba in Kuwait. By April the UAE had been targeted by more than 2,800 Iranian missiles and drones, more than any other country. On 18 March Iran hit Qatar's Ras Laffan gas plant after Israel struck South Pars. On 27 March an Iranian attack on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia wounded at least 12 US troops and damaged refuelling aircraft. In September the US sent two more Patriot batteries to Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

Hormuz and shipping: Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz stopped in the first days, with about 150 ships stalled on 1 March. On 27 March Iran moved to charge fees for passage. The US began a naval blockade of Iranian ports on 13 April and lifted it on 18 June. Iran attacked three ships in the strait on 7 July, and the US reimposed the blockade on 8 July. In the week of 28 September to 5 October at least 12 tankers were attacked around Hormuz, the most in any week of the war (the IMO counted nine incidents).

Talks and ceasefires: On 7 April Trump announced a two-week ceasefire from 8 April, mediated by Pakistan. Talks led by JD Vance opened in Islamabad on 11 April and ended on 12 April after 21 hours without a deal. A memorandum was signed digitally on 14 June and by Trump and Pezeshkian on 17 June; it collapsed on 8 July. In August, as its 60-day term lapsed, Oman and Qatar mediated. Indirect talks were held at the UN on 22 September; Trump rejected Iran's seven-day ceasefire offer on 26 September, and on 6 October Qatar said messages were again passing between the two sides.

Sanctions and the economy: The US Treasury began its "Economic Fury" sanctions on 15 April and "Operation Economic Outcast" on 24 August. Brent crude averaged $70.89 a barrel in February, $117.29 in April, $83.76 in July and $114.16 in September (EIA). The IEA put Gulf oil exports at about 13 million barrels a day in August, against about 24 million before the war.
